source: maintainer decision 2026-11-22 (what can be computed is not configured); the properties review, items 1-4, 7
statement: What a snapshot source's options once took as settings is computed, from the revalidation interval, the pipeline's timeout and the machine, and the starter has no property for it: a document unconfirmed for 6 revalidation intervals is logged at WARN and for 30 at ERROR as stale, so a lag report is a count of missed passes and the warning threshold is always above the interval; a cold load waits 40 % of `cosec.pipeline.timeout` (never below a millisecond), so it never waits as long as the request it serves; the compile threads are one per 2 cores, between 1 and 4 (a four-core pod keeps the two threads `ColdBurstBenchmark` measured); a revalidation pass confirms 16 documents at once. A key that once set one (`lag-warn`, `lag-escalate`, `cold-load-timeout`, `compile-threads`, `reload-concurrency`, `shadow.report-interval`, and the control plane's keys of `CTL-72`) fails startup as a key CoSec does not read, saying it is no longer a property and what replaced it. The starter says once at startup what it derived and from what.
guards: runtime:SnapshotOptionsDeriveTest#a lag threshold is a count of missed passes, always above the interval
runtime:SnapshotOptionsDeriveTest#a cold load waits less than the request it serves, for every deadline
runtime:SnapshotOptionsDeriveTest#the compile threads follow the cores, between one and four, and a four-core pod keeps the two measured
spring-boot:UnknownPropertiesTest#a removed key is said to be no longer a property, with what replaced it
spring-boot:DerivedSnapshotSettingsTest#the line says what was derived, from the interval, the deadline and the cores
